newsitem.title: CANADA: Aber says diamond mine may go deeper.
newsitem.headline: Aber says diamond mine may go deeper.

text.p: Aber Resources Ltd said on Tuesday it might be able to mine diamonds at greater depth than previously believed from the A-154 South kimberlite pipe at its Diavik diamond property in Canada's Northwest Territories.
Aber said in a news release Tuesday that drill holes this year encountered diamond-bearing rock at depths as great as 532 meters. Its previous resource modelling was based on a depth of 400 meters.
"Until now we've been indicating that we would be able to mine to a depth of 400 meters. This suggests we might be able to mine deeper," said Aber spokesman Alan Bayless.
Aber has 40 percent of the Diavik project and a unit of RTZ Corp Plc has the remainder.

Bayless said it was too early to assess what impact the latest information might have on the resource estimate for the property. An updated resource model for four kimberlite pipes on the property is due to be released near the end of July.
In its news release, Aber said five holes on A-154 South ranging from depths of 387 to 532 meters showed grades comparable to those in the upper portion of the pipe.
"The pipe remains consistent in its relative homogeniety and no barren zones were encountered," Aber said.
Aber expects to release valuations of diamonds recovered from large-diameter core drill holes in about a month.
Aber is expected to begin mining diamonds at the remote site in the Northwest Territories in 2001. Aber has said kimberlite pipes on the property are among the richest in the world.
Mining is expected to be conducted through an open pit although the potential for mining at greater depths raises the possibility of an underground operation in later stages.
